title: Posner spatial cueing
summary: Posner's (1980) central-cue experiment: a plus sign or an arrow at fixation, then 1000 ms later a white square 7° left or right, detected with one key. Arrows point to the square's side on 80% of target trials; the plus sign is uninformative. RT is faster after a valid cue (benefit) and slower after an invalid one (cost) than after the neutral cue, with the eyes held at fixation (checked by an eye tracker; a keyboard-only set runs without one). Catch trials have no square.
references: Posner, M. I. (1980). Orienting of attention. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 32(1), 3–25. https://doi.org/10.1080/00335558008248231

Posner, M. I., Nissen, M. J., & Ogden, W. C. (1978). Attended and unattended processing modes: The role of set for spatial location. In H. L. Pick & I. J. Saltzman (Eds.), Modes of perceiving and processing information (pp. 137–157). Erlbaum.

deviations.original: EOG; only trials on which the eyes stayed fixated were used, selected after the fact (p. 6)
deviations.here: A video eye tracker, when the rig has one (configs/task.yaml). Gaze leaving a window around fixation ends the attempt at once as FIXATION_BREAK, and the same trial is served again later in its block
deviations.reason: The same exclusion criterion, applied online. Serving the trial again keeps each block's planned 80-trial composition, so the cue validities stay exactly 0.8/0.2

deviations.here: configs/task-keyboard.yaml runs with no tracker. The subject is asked to keep fixation, but nothing checks it
deviations.reason: Lets a booth without a tracker run the task. Data from this set cannot rule out eye movements toward the cued side, so this set is not the original protocol; its menu name says it has no eye tracker

deviations.original: Luminance increments in a dark field (p. 6)
deviations.here: alhazen's mid-grey window, with a white square as the luminance increment
deviations.reason: alhazen 2.16 fixes the window colour at mid-grey and has no per-task background. Drawing a dark field inside each trial would flash grey between trials. The increment's contrast therefore differs from the original

deviations.original: Not described in Posner (1980); the primary report (Posner, Nissen & Ogden, 1978) was not read
deviations.here: A computer monitor. Sizes are in degrees of visual angle from the rig file's geometry, and every duration is rounded to whole display frames
deviations.reason: The original apparatus is not available. A frame-locked monitor times every interval to within one frame

assumed.value: 0.3 dva diameter
assumed.reason: Not stated. A conventional small fixation point

assumed.item: Fixation point during the inter-trial interval
assumed.value: A dot at the centre during the inter-trial interval, replaced by the cue at cue onset and shown again for feedback
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 (p. 6) shows only the cue at the centre. A fixation mark is needed for the subject (and the tracker) to fixate before the cue

assumed.value: 1.0 dva (arrow length; plus-sign arm span)
assumed.reason: Not stated. Large enough to read at the fovea without moving the eyes

assumed.value: 0.12 dva
assumed.reason: Not stated. A clearly visible line at a 1-dva cue size

assumed.value: A horizontal shaft with a chevron head (two strokes at 45° to the shaft, a third of its length) at the pointing end
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 draws a simple arrow without dimensions

assumed.value: 1.0 dva square
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 draws a filled square but gives no size

assumed.value: White (maximum luminance) for the fixation point, cue and target
assumed.reason: The paper says only 'clear above threshold luminance increments' (p. 6). White gives the largest increment the display allows

assumed.value: Uniform between 1000 and 2000 ms, drawn per trial
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 (p. 6) gives the range 1000–2000 ms but not how values were drawn

assumed.value: 1000 ms after target onset
assumed.reason: Not stated. Fig. 1 shows the target lasting until the response; the deadline only ends trials with no response. Simple RTs in the paper are about 250–300 ms (Fig. 2, p. 7)

assumed.value: Space bar
assumed.reason: The paper says a single key pressed wherever the stimulus occurred (pp. 6–7), not which key

assumed.value: 25% of trials show the cue and no target; a key press is a FALSE_ALARM
assumed.reason: Posner (1980) does not mention catch trials for this experiment. 25% is the catch-trial rate the same paper reports for the central-cue detection task of Shulman, Remington & McLean (p. 10). Catch trials stop a simple-RT subject from responding to the clock

assumed.value: 1000 ms (the response deadline), counted from the moment the target would have appeared
assumed.reason: Follows from the assumed catch trials; nothing in the paper

assumed.item: Share of arrow and neutral cues
assumed.value: 50% arrow (25% left, 25% right), 50% neutral plus sign
assumed.reason: The paper gives the cue validities (p. 6) but not how often each cue type occurred

assumed.value: 80 (24 valid, 6 invalid, 30 neutral, 20 catch; left and right balanced)
assumed.reason: Not stated. 80 is the smallest block that gives exact 0.8/0.2 validity, 0.5/0.5 neutral sides, 50% arrow cues and 25% catch trials with left and right balanced

assumed.value: 4 (320 trials, about 20 minutes)
assumed.reason: Not stated. Gives 96 valid, 24 invalid and 120 neutral target trials per subject

assumed.value: All cue types intermixed, shuffled within each block
assumed.reason: The paper cues every trial (p. 8) but does not say whether neutral and arrow trials were mixed or blocked

assumed.value: A rest break between blocks
assumed.reason: Not stated. A convention for a 20-minute RT session

assumed.value: A key press during the cue-target interval ends the attempt as ANTICIPATION; the trial is served again later in the block
assumed.reason: Not stated. Keeps premature responses out of the RTs and the block composition intact

assumed.value: No key by the deadline on a target trial is a MISS: completed, counted, not served again
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.value: Target-trial RTs under 100 ms are left out of the RT means
assumed.reason: Not stated. A common lower bound for simple RT

assumed.value: For the 500 ms feedback period the fixation point turns green (detection, correct rejection) or red (miss, false alarm, anticipation, fixation break); no RT is shown
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 (p. 6) shows a 500-ms feedback period but not what it showed. alhazen's standard trial feedback is used

assumed.value: Off (display.feedback_beeps: false in both rig files)
assumed.reason: The paper mentions no tone. alhazen would otherwise beep with the feedback

assumed.value: 1.5 dva radius around the fixation point
assumed.reason: The paper used EOG and gives no criterion for 'remained fixated' (p. 6). 1.5 dva is well inside the 7-dva target eccentricity, so any saccade toward a target position breaks fixation

assumed.value: Gaze must enter the window before the inter-trial interval starts; after 5 s without it the attempt ends as NO_FIXATION and is served again
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.value: From fixation acquisition until the response or the deadline
assumed.reason: The paper does not say over which part of the trial the eyes had to stay fixated

assumed.value: None built in. alhazen's test mode cannot shorten this design (each block is already one pass through the 80 cells), so for practice run test mode with a copy of the params file set to paradigm.blocks.n_blocks: 1 (80 trials, about 5 minutes)
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.value: The wording in instructions.md
assumed.reason: The paper gives no instructions text

tasks.title: Posner spatial cueing
tasks.summary: Fixation point, 1000–2000 ms; cue (+, ← or →) at fixation; square 7° left or right 1000 ms later (or nothing, on catch trials); one key; 500 ms feedback.

parameters.name: fixation_control
parameters.label: Fixation control
parameters.meaning: "tracker": gaze must stay in the fixation window and a break serves the trial again (the paper's EOG control, p. 6). "none": the keyboard-only set, nothing checks fixation (configs/task-keyboard.yaml; not the original protocol).

parameters.name: fixation_window_dva
parameters.label: Fixation window radius
parameters.meaning: Radius of the window gaze must stay inside, eye-tracker set only. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: acquire_timeout
parameters.label: Fixation acquisition timeout
parameters.meaning: How long the fixation point waits for gaze before the attempt is served again. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: fix_size_dva
parameters.label: Fixation point size
parameters.meaning: Diameter of the fixation point. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: cue_size_dva
parameters.label: Cue size
parameters.meaning: Arrow length and plus-sign arm span. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: cue_stroke_dva
parameters.label: Cue stroke width
parameters.meaning: Width of the cue's strokes. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: target_size_dva
parameters.label: Target size
parameters.meaning: Side of the filled square. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: target_ecc_dva
parameters.label: Target eccentricity
parameters.meaning: Distance of the square's centre from fixation, left or right on the horizontal meridian. Paper: 7°, Fig. 1 and Fig. 2.

parameters.name: stimulus_color
parameters.label: Stimulus colour
parameters.meaning: Colour of the fixation point, cue and square, -1..1 per channel. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: intertrial_min
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval, shortest
parameters.meaning: Shortest inter-trial interval before the cue. Paper: 1000 ms, Fig. 1 (drawn uniformly: assumed).

parameters.name: intertrial_max
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval, longest
parameters.meaning: Longest inter-trial interval before the cue. Paper: 2000 ms, Fig. 1.

parameters.name: cue_target_soa
parameters.label: Cue-target SOA
parameters.meaning: From cue onset to the square's onset. Paper: 1000 ms, Fig. 1.

parameters.name: cue_stays_on
parameters.label: Cue stays on
parameters.meaning: Whether the cue stays on screen with the square. Paper: Fig. 1 draws them together.

parameters.name: response_deadline
parameters.label: Response deadline
parameters.meaning: How long a key is accepted after the square appears (or would have, on a catch trial). ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: feedback_duration
parameters.label: Feedback duration
parameters.meaning: How long the fixation point shows green or red. Paper: 500 ms, Fig. 1.

parameters.name: response_key
parameters.label: Response key
parameters.meaning: The single detection key. The paper says one key, not which. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: design.validity
parameters.label: Arrow validity
parameters.meaning: Probability that the square is on the side an arrow points to, on target trials. Paper: 0.8, p. 6.

parameters.name: design.arrow_fraction
parameters.label: Share of arrow cues
parameters.meaning: Fraction of trials with an arrow; the rest have the plus sign. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: design.catch_fraction
parameters.label: Catch-trial share
parameters.meaning: Fraction of trials behind every cue type with no square. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: design.trials_per_block
parameters.label: Trials per block
parameters.meaning: One block's fixed composition, served shuffled; the proportions above must divide it into whole trials. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.blocks.n_blocks
parameters.label: Blocks
parameters.meaning: Number of blocks, with a rest between them. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

outcomes.name: DETECTED
outcomes.meaning: The key after the square appeared; rt_ms is the reaction time.

outcomes.name: MISS
outcomes.meaning: No key by the deadline on a target trial.

outcomes.name: CORRECT_REJECTION
outcomes.meaning: No key on a catch trial.

outcomes.name: FALSE_ALARM
outcomes.meaning: A key on a catch trial.

outcomes.name: ANTICIPATION
outcomes.meaning: A key during the cue-target interval; the trial is served again later in the block.

outcomes.name: FIXATION_BREAK
outcomes.meaning: Eye-tracker set: gaze left the fixation window (or was lost) before the response; served again.

outcomes.name: NO_FIXATION
outcomes.meaning: Eye-tracker set: gaze never reached the fixation window; served again.

events.name: FIX_ON
events.meaning: Fixation point shown (start of the inter-trial interval, keyboard set; start of acquisition, eye-tracker set).

events.name: FIX_ACQUIRED
events.meaning: Gaze reached the fixation window; the inter-trial interval starts (eye-tracker set).

events.name: CUE_ON
events.meaning: The cue replaced the fixation point.

events.name: EARLY_RESPONSE
events.meaning: A key during the cue-target interval (an anticipation).

events.name: TARGET_ON
events.meaning: The square appeared; reaction time runs from this flip.

events.name: CATCH_ON
events.meaning: Catch trials: the moment the square would have appeared.
